speaker: Doctor
text: That's an unusual presentation for weakness and sensory loss in just the right arm. To narrow this down, can you tell me exactly where the numbness and weakness start, and do you have any history of neck pain or trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of anabolic steroid use and unexplained weight loss, we need to rule out metastatic disease or a paraneoplastic syndrome affecting the brachial plexus. REQUEST TEST: MRI Cervical Spine with contrast, REQUEST TEST: Chest CT, and REQUEST IMAGES of the right brachial plexus. Do you have any night sweats or fevers?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI Cervical Spine with contrast: Pending; Chest CT: Solid mass at the apex of the right lung, suggestive of a tumor; Right brachial plexus images: Pending. Additional findings from current workup: Temperature 99.5°F (37.5°C); Blood Pressure 177/108 mmHg; Heart Rate 90/min; Respiratory Rate 17/min; Oxygen Saturation 98% on room air. Neurological Exam: 2/5 strength in the right arm, 5/5 strength in the left arm; Decreased sensation in the right arm; Normal reflexes; Unaffected coordination. Labs: Complete Blood Count (WBC, Hemoglobin, Platelets) within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
text: The Chest CT shows a solid mass at the apex of your right lung; combined with your weight loss, night sweats, and severe arm weakness, this is highly suggestive of a Pancoast tumor (superior sulcus tumor) causing a Pancoast syndrome. Do you have any difficulty turning your head to the right or shoulder pain radiating down the side of your arm?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness in the right arm. I also have Decreased sensation in the right arm, Dull aching and burning pain in the right arm, Significant weight loss.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast Tumor (Superior Sulcus Tumor) causing Pancoast Syndrome with right brachial plexus invasion. The apical lung mass explains the specific distribution of weakness and sensory loss in your right arm, along with the significant weight loss. We will need to proceed with staging and likely surgical consultation or radiation therapy planning.
